breakdown_seconds_per_video_hour.remainder_note: head sliding-window inference (536 ONNX calls at window 64) plus array handling; measured by difference, not directly

comparison.verdict: confirmed for what it measured, and it is not the end-to-end figure
comparison.why: The 49 is the benchmark arm's embedding pass over pre-extracted JPEG crops; it never decodes a video. The model work here is 27 + 12 = 39 s/video-hour, consistent with it. The pipeline additionally decodes 20 minutes of 4K, which costs 386 s/video-hour and is 74% of the total.
comparison.decode_is_not_avoidable_by_striding: decode at 1 fps 386 s vs at the 2 s stride 381 s - ffmpeg decodes every frame regardless of the fps filter, so sampling less does not decode less
comparison.batching_the_backbone_is_not_the_lever: 12 -> 10 s/video-hour. The backbone is 2% of the run.

output.caveat: W1 is one of the three windows the shipped head trained on, so these totals are IN-SAMPLE and are evidence that the path runs end to end, not evidence of accuracy. Every accuracy figure belongs to the cross-validated folds and lives in the model card.
